routes.name: Short stay without a visa (Schengen rules)
routes.summary: Citizens of countries on Slovakia's visa-exempt list (for example the US, UK, Canada, Japan, Australia) can enter without a visa. The usual Schengen limit is 90 days in any 180.

other: Check the official visa-exempt list by nationality. Some countries need a biometric passport. ETIAS will apply to visa-exempt travelers once it starts.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss citizen rights
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens can stay 3 months with just an ID card or passport. Longer stays need registration of residence with the Foreign Police. Family members have similar rights.

other: Longer stays need registration. Permanent residence for EU citizens and their family members is a separate step.

routes.name: Temporary residence for employment (single permit)
routes.summary: Residence and work permit for a specific job. The Labour Office first confirms the vacancy can't be filled locally. Temporary residence is tied to one purpose only.

other: The Labour Office (UPSVaR) must confirm the vacancy can be filled by a third-country national, unless an exemption applies.
Documents include work permit or employer confirmation, clean criminal record extract (not older than 90 days) and proof of housing.
Income and fee amounts were not on the pages read.

routes.processing: Decision within 90 days. 60 days for the standard employment route, and 30 days for jobs in shortage occupations in the region.

routes.name: EU Blue Card
routes.summary: For highly qualified employment. Needs a contract of at least one year and a salary of at least 1.5 times the average monthly wage in the sector. Issued for three years, or the shorter contract length plus 90 days.

other: Education requirements were not on the page.

routes.name: Temporary residence for business
routes.summary: For people running a business in Slovakia. Since 1 July 2025, applications can only be filed at Slovak embassies abroad, with no exceptions. You need a business plan and proof that it can work, plus two bank balances (one personal, one for the business).

other: Business account balance must be 20 times the living minimum for the standard route, 100 times for a business plan route, or 40 times for an innovative project. Living minimum amount in EUR was not confirmed.
Needs a clean criminal record extract, a business plan on the Ministry of Economy template, and proof of purpose of stay (all not older than 90 days).

routes.name: Temporary residence for study
routes.summary: Temporary residence for study, granted for the expected length of studies. Apply in person at a Slovak embassy, or at the Foreign Police if you are already legally in Slovakia.

other: Needs confirmation of admission from the school or a program body, clean criminal record extract and proof of purpose (not older than 90 days).

routes.name: Temporary residence for family reunification
routes.summary: Family reunification is a listed temporary residence purpose. Applications are decided within 90 days, extendable by 30.

other: Needs marriage or birth certificates, proof of the sponsor's residence and clean criminal record extract (not needed for children under 14).
Income and fee amounts were not read.

routes.name: Permanent residence
routes.summary: Permanent residence for 5 years is for certain family members of Slovak citizens, some children and cases in Slovakia's interest. After at least 4 years of this, you can apply for unlimited permanent residence.

other: Exact conditions for each 5-year category were not read. Decision within 90 days.

routes.name: Long-term residence (EU long-term resident)
routes.summary: Long-term residence needs stable and regular income for you and your family, housing and health insurance. Decision within 90 days of a complete application.

other: Income can be shown with an employment contract, employer letter, bank balance or pension. Five years of continuous residence is the usual EU rule, but the page read did not state it.

routes.name: Tolerated residence
routes.summary: Granted for up to 180 days per period when expulsion is blocked, for minors found in Slovakia, trafficking victims and similar cases. Holders can't carry out business. This is not asylum, so check the Ministry of Interior for the asylum process.

routes.name: Citizenship by naturalization
routes.summary: Standard route is 8 consecutive years of permanent residence right before applying, a clean criminal record, Slovak language (spoken and written) and general knowledge of Slovakia. Shorter periods apply to some groups.

eligibility.language: Slovak, spoken and written, plus general knowledge of Slovakia (language not tested under age 14)
other: Must be in good standing on taxes, health insurance and social contributions.

Shorter routes: 4 years after asylum, 3 years for people with Slovak Living Abroad status, 3 years if born in Slovakia, 10 years of residence with permanent residence granted, and cases of significant benefit to Slovakia.

sources.label: MZV Slovakia, Slovak citizenship

citizenship.note: Slovak citizens lose their citizenship if they voluntarily acquire another, with exceptions such as acquiring it through marriage to a foreigner, at birth, or before 17 July 2010. The page read does not say whether naturalizing foreigners must give up their old citizenship.

routes.name: Citizenship by marriage
routes.summary: Married to a Slovak citizen, still married, and living together in a shared household in Slovakia for at least 5 years right before applying. This replaces the 8 year permanent residence requirement.

other: The general conditions still apply: clean criminal record, no pending expulsion, Slovak language and knowledge of Slovakia, and taxes and insurance in order.

sources.label: MZV Slovakia, Slovak citizenship

routes.name: Citizenship by birth or descent
routes.summary: A child gets Slovak citizenship at birth if at least one parent is a Slovak citizen. Also for children born in Slovakia to stateless parents, or to foreign parents whose citizenship the child does not get.

other: The page does not say how many generations back descent goes. Former Slovak citizens can also apply for citizenship on special grounds.

sources.label: MZV Slovakia, Slovak citizenship

citizenship.note: A child born abroad to a Slovak parent is a citizen at birth. Adult dual citizenship is limited, because Slovaks lose citizenship when they voluntarily take another.

routes.name: National visa (D, stays over 3 months)
routes.summary: A national visa covers a stay over 3 months and up to 1 year. It is used when needed alongside a residence permit application or for language school with at least 25 lessons a week (age 15 and up).

other: Needs a valid passport (valid at least 90 days after leaving), photo, proof of purpose and health insurance for the whole visa.
Not used for temporary residence for business. Apply at a Slovak embassy.

documents: Passport valid at least 90 days after leaving
Health insurance for the visa period

routes.name: Permanent residence for an unlimited period
routes.summary: Available after at least 4 years of 5-year permanent residence. Also for children under 18 of someone who has it. Apply in person at the Foreign Police.

other: Needs a valid passport, health insurance and proof of housing (not older than 90 days), and a statement that the reasons for residence still apply.
Decision within 90 days of a complete application.

routes.name: Temporary residence for Slovaks Living Abroad
routes.summary: For foreign nationals who hold Slovak Living Abroad status. After 3 continuous years of residence in Slovakia, they can apply for citizenship.

other: Requires an issued Slovak Living Abroad certificate. Conditions for that status were not read.
